contents.entry: The cancel set: fourteen tickets, by rule not by list
Bootstrap state: the only writer of bootstrap:state
How it starts without an agent typing
Every wait, its timeout and its fallback
What this volume needs from the shared volumes

pointers.sibling: Input and output record schema of this node
Unlanded cleanup, which carries every other row
Cleanup registry and runs, which deletes the design branch
pointers.shared: The book is the canonical design (D14)
SPEC-16 and SPEC-17 as sources, never authority
Bootstrap states B0 to B8; this node is the only writer of bootstrap:state
Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book

purpose.is: Writes the three cut-over records the D09 and D14 rulings call for, at GOFACTORY: cancel records for the fourteen SPEC-16 build tickets, a close record for PR 35, and a delete record for the SPEC-16 design branch once the small Go cut has taken the files it needs.
purpose.is-not: It does not cut the small-cut tickets (N-17 and N-18 do, from the G1 and G2 volumes) and it does not delete anything itself (N-45 does, from its branch.delete record).
purpose.why: HANDOFF ruling 27: small Go cut on the same proto, keep interfaces and fake clock, cancel the fourteen SPEC-16 tickets; cancels and the small-cut tickets land only at GOFACTORY through the normal ticket path. 04-UNLANDED section 2: PR 35 is DECIDE D14 then CLOSE; D14 is ruled (C42, the owner from the phone).

input.record: The GOFACTORY ruling record: the owner word matched by N-29 from an owner principal on the owner page or the owner CLI (shared/authority.xml#owner-words); never a relay, a default, an import or seat text.

The D09 ruling (card C41) and the D14 ruling (card C42). The answers.jsonl rows imported at bring-up are evidence only (source import); they authorize nothing on their own. They count as rulings once the GOFACTORY card, which lists C41 and C42 and the cut-over they cause (fourteen cancels, PR 35 closed, design branch deleted after harvest), is answered GOFACTORY by the owner: that one owner answer is the authority for this node's records.
Merges of small-cut tickets whose declared files came from the design branch (the ticket carries source_branch and source_sha); the design branch delete waits on the last of them.

output.record: One per ticket in the cancel set: ticket id, full title from the ticket file, reason (D09 ruling id), the epic it belongs to, and the ticket.request id for the archive PR.
PR 35: number, title, head sha, the closing comment text (D14 ruling id, the book's path as the canonical design), the treehouse slot 2 lease released.

feat/go-scheduler-design-one-xml-spec-per-domain-unde: the sha at deletion (012fa41 expected; the record carries the actual), the tag rebuild/spec-16-design-<date> made first, the list of small-cut tickets that harvested files from it.
The cancel set did not count fourteen (reason cancel-set-mismatch); nothing is cancelled; the record names the set found and the rule that produced it; owner acts through one card.
bootstrap:state moved one state (from, to, the proof record ids cited), written in the same Commit as the entity CAS.
The B1 proof: the passing store, schema and fixture tests on the test state root.
The B7 proof: the proof records of cut-over steps 2, 6 and 7, each named; the owner-only ready card follows (no default, no deadline).

cancel-set.rule: The set is computed, not typed: every child ticket of epic WO-20261012-ea33 - Go scheduler: a lightweight Go service in Podman on WSL schedules the small loop and the software factory DAG, designed by a Fable architect and built by four Opus workers, with status ready on main at the GOFACTORY sha, minus any child that 04-UNLANDED.md gives its own verdict row (WO-20261012-8d87 - Replay fixtures: one golden case per routes row and per policies row under scheduler/testdata/replay, derived from the factory suite's cases, synthetic, with a schema and a check script, which is a KEEP row in section 3 and goes through N-49), minus the epic itself.
cancel-set.expected: Fourteen: WO-20261012-9790 (config), 5a3d (intake), 32fe (routes), 7a9a (job), 8e69 (seat), 6e43 (policy), 3c7a (health), d7f4 (executor), b12c (observe and status), 1ccf (engine and run, check, retry), fa36 (cut-over and shadow mode), 379f (contract tests), 0113 (lint and CI wiring), 1635 (end-to-end acceptance). Full titles are taken from the ticket files at cancel time and written into the records; L14 section 4.1 truncates them.
cancel-set.check: If the computed count is not fourteen, the node writes cancel 412 cancel-set-mismatch and one card with the set it found; the owner's answer is a ruling that names the set, and the node re-runs on it. A count mismatch is a sign the tree moved since the investigation, which the owner must see, never a reason to cancel more or fewer silently.
cancel-set.what-cancel-means: A cancel record is the ticket's status in the store (D04 C). While ticket files still live under work-orders/ on main, one ticket request to N-03 archives the fourteen files as cancelled with the reason (the normal ticket path, one small PR touching only those files and the index), so main and the store agree. The archive ticket declares exactly those files.

bootstrap.s: N-50 is the only writer of entity bootstrap:state (contracts.schema.json#/$defs/bootstrap_state, shared/cut-over.xml#bootstrap). On every scheduler tick it reads the state and the proof records its exit names; when they are all present it advances one state by compare-and-swap, in one Commit (operation key N-50/bootstrap.advance/<to-state>/r1) that writes the entity and bootstrap.advanced 200 citing the proof ids; never two states at once, never backwards.

B1: when the foundation tests pass on the test state root, bootstrap.foundation 201 lists them. B1 to B2 needs that record and the GOFACTORY ruling, the owner word typed by the owner into the owner CLI (coq bootstrap authorize) or the owner page, never a relay or an import. B6 to B7: bootstrap.ready 201 names the proofs of steps 2, 6 and 7. B7 to B8: only the USERGO ruling; N-44 clears flag:hold on the same ruling.
N-50 never writes a flag and never matches an owner word: N-29 matches the words, N-44 writes flag:hold, N-50 moves the state; a ruling from any other principal or source moves nothing.

mechanism.where: Go package cutover in the service; forge calls through the service's gh auth; file reads from the mirror at the GOFACTORY sha.
mechanism.step: On GOFACTORY: verify the ruling's principal is the owner and its source the owner page or CLI, and that the GOFACTORY card listed the D09 and D14 rulings (card ids C41 and C42); if either is missing from the card, write cancel 412 reason ruling-missing and one owner card; nothing else runs. A ruling from any other principal or source applies nothing (N-29 refuses it 403 upstream).
Compute the cancel set (rule above) from the ticket files at the sha; write one cancel 200 per ticket, idempotent by key cancel:<ticket>; write one ticket.request for the archive PR.

PR 35: gh pr close 35 --comment with the text; release the treehouse slot lease (slot 2) through N-45 with a disposition pointing at N-49's entry U02-35; write pr.close 200. Its branch is then a CLOSE row for N-45 (the record carries the branch name and sha).

Design branch: wait until every merged small-cut ticket that names source_branch feat/go-scheduler-design-one-xml-spec-per-domain-unde has its merge record, and no open small-cut ticket names it; then tag rebuild/spec-16-design-<YYYYMMDD> at the branch sha (history kept), write branch.delete 200, and N-45 deletes the branch on that record.
The two kept worktrees (~/.cache/wt-sched, ~/.cache/wt-sched-w3) are N-49 section 6 rows whose trigger is this node's branch.delete and N-49's replay-fixtures re-verdict.

diagram.mermaid: flowchart LR G[GOFACTORY ruling] --> V{D09 + D14 rulings present?} V -- no --> M[cancel 412 + one card] V -- yes --> S[compute cancel set at sha] S --> C{count == 14?} C -- no --> X[cancel 412 + one card] C -- yes --> R[14 cancel records + archive ticket.request] G --> P[gh pr close 35 + slot 2 release] --> Q[pr.close 200] G --> W[wait: small-cut merges naming the design branch] W --> T[tag then branch.delete 200] --> N45[N-45 deletes]

start.s: The GOFACTORY ruling record starts it; the D09 and D14 rulings are already records; the small-cut merges are records; nobody types a cancel verb and nobody closes PR 35 by hand.

wait.what: the D09 and D14 ruling records
wait.timeout: PT0S: checked once when the GOFACTORY ruling arrives, never waited on
wait.fallback: cancel 412 and one card; GOFACTORY's other nodes (N-49) proceed
ladder 10, 30, 90 s; then 423 and an alert; N-49's entry for PR 35 stays planned and the daily retry applies

wait.what: small-cut merges naming the design branch
wait.fallback: branch.delete 423 reason harvest-late with the open tickets named; one card: delete anyway (the tag keeps history) or extend; default after 7 more days is delete, because the tag holds every file. This card is not owner-only: its default is a system branch delete already authorized by the GOFACTORY answer, never an owner word or a break glass.
N-11's dead path for the ticket; the cancel records are already the truth in the store; the file status lags, which N-51's audit shows as a known row, not a failure

waits.cog-test: The cog that could stall this node is a human waiting to be sure the small cut took every file it needs. The tag removes the risk: a deleted branch's files are one git show away.

retries.policy: Forge calls and store puts; cancel records are idempotent by key.
retries.recover: After three failures the record is 423 with the error; the daily tick retries transient classes for 7 days; the cancel set is never partially applied silently: each ticket's record stands alone and the archive ticket lists exactly the ones recorded.
retries.report: Each 412 and the w3 timeout are one card each; 423 is an alert record.

many-agents.readers: Small-cut workers read their own tickets; none reads this volume to know what is cancelled, because a cancelled ticket is never dispatched (N-07 reads the store status).
many-agents.writers: One run under lease cutover:run; records are idempotent by key, so a second GOFACTORY traversal (refused upstream anyway) would write nothing new.
many-agents.collision: A small-cut ticket starting on a file from the design branch while the branch delete runs: the ticket's workspace is a worktree from origin/main plus a git show of the source sha, never a checkout of the branch; the tag exists before the delete; nothing a seat reads disappears.

N-49's section 3 row for the design branch and this node's branch.delete: N-49 marks that row as owned by N-50 (action re-verdict, result_ref the branch.delete id) and never emits its own disposition for it.

The archive ticket and another ticket touching work-orders/ at once: one file, one in-flight ticket; the archive ticket declares exactly the fourteen files plus the index, and N-14 refuses an overlap.
A worker that was dispatched on one of the fourteen before GOFACTORY: impossible, the line is held; after GOFACTORY N-07 reads the cancel status before any dispatch.

status-codes.emits: Ticket cancelled in the store; system acts (archive ticket).
Cancel set count not fourteen (cancel-set-mismatch); owner acts (one card naming the set).
D09 or D14 ruling missing from the GOFACTORY card (ruling-missing); owner acts (one card).
bootstrap:state moved one state; system acts (the steps the new state allows).
B1 proof present; nobody acts until GOFACTORY.
B7 reached; owner acts (USERGO on the owner-only ready card).
The archive ticket of the fourteen cancels, to N-03.
Design branch tagged and marked for deletion; N-45 acts.
PR close failed after 3 attempts at the forge; system acts (daily retry).
Branch delete failed after 3 attempts at the forge, or harvest-late (w3); system acts (daily retry) or owner acts (w3 card).

state-paths.path: The computed set with full titles at the GOFACTORY sha.

edges.in: merge (small-cut tickets naming the design branch; a store query, not a drawn edge)
edges.out: branch.delete; the PR 35 branch and slot through N-49's entry

item.check: The cancel set computed on main at GOFACTORY counts fourteen and matches the expected ids.
item.proof: The cancel-set JSON file and fourteen cancel 200 records with full titles; a test world with fifteen ready children yields cancel 412 cancel-set-mismatch and one card.

item.check: PR 35 is closed with the comment naming D14 and the book.
item.proof: gh pr view 35 --json state,comments shows CLOSED and the comment; pr.close 200.

item.check: The design branch is tagged before deletion and deleted only after the harvest.
item.proof: git tag -l rebuild/spec-16-design-* non-empty; branch.delete 200 lists the harvesting tickets; N-45 cleanup.run row for the branch with the sha.

item.check: bootstrap:state moves one state at a time, only on its proofs, and only N-50 writes it.
item.proof: A test world at B3 with the step 3 proof: one bootstrap.advanced 200 to B4 citing it; a control.resume ruling at B4 moves nothing; a Commit to bootstrap:state from another principal is 403 kind_not_permitted.

item.check: A missing ruling record stops the node with 412.
item.proof: A test world without the C41 record; cancel 412; no cancel records; one card.

item.check: No cancelled ticket is ever dispatched.
item.proof: N-07 test: a ticket with a cancel record is not in the ready set after the next tick.

item.check: Main and the store agree on the fourteen.
item.proof: The archive PR merged: the fourteen files under work-orders/archive with status cancelled and the D09 reason; N-51's audit shows no status lag row for them.

may.do: compute the set; write cancel, pr.close, branch.delete; advance bootstrap:state on its proofs; close PR 35; tag the design branch; request the archive ticket
answer GOFACTORY (owner page or CLI); rule a different cancel set on the cancel-set-mismatch card; rule on the w3 card

may-not.do: cancel a ticket; close a PR; delete or tag a branch
carry GOFACTORY or the cancel-set answer; a relayed or imported answer authorizes nothing here
cancel outside the computed set; delete the design branch before the tag exists; delete before the harvest or the w3 default

monitoring.counter: open or closed, from the forge snapshot.
present, tagged, deleted; and the count of open small-cut tickets naming it.
monitoring.panel: The R-04 row shows PR 35 closed and the branch state.

runbook.step: Read the set found; if the tree moved (a ticket was done or re-cut), answer with the set to cancel; the ruling re-runs the node.
The GOFACTORY card did not list C41 or C42: N-28 posts a fresh GOFACTORY card that lists both, and the owner answers it on the owner page or CLI; no system lane writes a ruling for the owner.
Delete anyway (the tag keeps the files) or extend; the default is delete after 7 more days.

step.when: a file from the deleted branch is needed later

runbook.step: git show rebuild/spec-16-design-<date>:<path> from the mirror; no branch restore needed.
runbook.cold-start: Records are in the store; the node re-runs idempotently on the GOFACTORY ruling at start.

D14 D: a new rebuild design; PR 35 closed; SPEC-17 and its draft become sources

Ruling 27: cancels and the small-cut tickets land only at GOFACTORY through the normal ticket path
The fourteen unbuilt tickets under work-orders/WO-20261010-329d/WO-20261012-ea33/ (fifteen lines listed; 8d87 has its own verdict)
PR 35: DECIDE D14 then CLOSE; its slot 2 lease goes with it
go-scheduler-design KEEP until D09; under D09 B keep only what the cut packages need, then delete
Each ticket takes its file from this branch at 012fa41; delete after the last build ticket merges
Rulings a gate checks are records; post via the record path before any node reads them
R-04: PR 35 landed, superseded or closed with a reason

reject.source: a typed list of fourteen ids as the cancel set
reject.reason: A list drifts (L14 lists fifteen lines); the set is computed from the epic's children at the sha and checked against fourteen, with a card on mismatch.

reject.source: deleting the design branch at GOFACTORY
reject.reason: The small cut takes files from it (D09 B); the tag plus the harvest wait keeps the files reachable without a hand restore.

reject.source: cancelling by editing the fourteen ticket files on main by hand
reject.reason: A hand line operation; the store status is the truth (D04 C) and the archive PR goes through the normal path (ruling 27).

reject.source: D09 option A (build as written) and C (freeze until the slice runs)
SPEC-17 1.0.1, its 1.1.0 draft and PR 35's v2.0 export as authority
reject.reason: D14: sources only; listed in shared/rejected-with-reason.xml by the shared author.

shared-needs.need: principles.xml#design-first naming the book as the canonical design (D14) and the sentence the PR 35 closing comment carries.

shared/rejected-with-reason.xml#spec-16 and #spec-17 entries for the SPEC-16 domain specs, SPEC-17 1.0.1, the 1.1.0 draft and PR 35's export, each with the reason and what was harvested (proto, interfaces, fake clock, H01 to H26, B1 to B10).
ticket status values including cancelled with reason and ruling id; a query for children of an epic by status at a sha; leases cutover:run.
cancel, pr.close, branch.delete, ruling (with card_id and decision), ticket.request, merge (with source_branch and source_sha on the ticket).
200, 412 cancel-set-mismatch or ruling-missing (owner acts), 423; bootstrap.advanced 200, bootstrap.foundation 201, bootstrap.ready 201.

answers.jsonl rows C34 to C42 and rulings-r02.jsonl rows C43 to C58 are imported at bring-up as evidence (source import, keyed by card id), never as owner answers; the GOFACTORY card lists the ones this node acts on.
Small-cut tickets carry source_branch and source_sha when their files come from the design branch.
cutover.epic WO-20261012-ea33, cutover.expected_count 14, cutover.harvest_timeout P14D, cutover.harvest_default_days 7, cutover.pr 35.
